## Hard rules
* Fleet package `src/herzchen/fleet/runner/` must contain NO identifier or non-docstring string that matches /otto|megado/i
  (tests/test_herzchen_boundary.py::test_fleet_carries_no_otto_or_megado_names) and imports nothing from `otto`.
* Do NOT edit: src/otto/hostctl/heavy.py, src/herzchen/fleet/capacity.py, src/herzchen/fleet/custody.py, any existing test.
* Do not git add `.runner-design.md` or `.brief.md`. Do not git stash. Do not commit unless told to.

## Package layout (src/herzchen/fleet/runner/)
* `__init__.py`  re-exports: Runner, ResultStore, StoreError, RunnerClient, RunnerUnavailable, RunnerServer, pick, Entry, Holder, git_commit_identity, EXIT_UNKNOWN
* `store.py`     ResultStore (below)
* `admission.py` pure queue/backfill rule
* `commit.py`    git_commit_identity
* `runner.py`    Runner core
* `server.py`    RunnerServer (unix socket, JSON lines) + `main(argv)`; `__main__.py` calls `server.main()`
* `client.py`    RunnerClient

## store.py — ResultStore(root, *, forbidden_roots=())
* Layout `root/runs/<run_id>.json` (0600), `root/seal.key` (0600, 32 random bytes created if absent), `root/output/`, root dir 0700.
* `forbidden_roots`: iterable of paths. Constructing a store whose realpath is inside (or equal to) any forbidden root raises `StoreError`. Re-checked on every `put`.
* `binding(argv, cwd, commit) -> str`: sha256 hex of canonical JSON `{"argv":[...],"cwd":cwd,"commit":commit}` (sort_keys, compact separators).
* A record is a dict. `seal` = HMAC-SHA256(key, canonical JSON of the record without the `seal` key), hex.
* `put(record)`: validates run_id against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; atomic write (tmp + fsync + os.replace, mode 0600); sets `seal`.
  Refuses (StoreError) to overwrite an existing file that (a) is unreadable/invalid-sealed, or (b) holds a terminal state (`settled` or `unknown`). Allowed transitions only: new->queued|running|settled|unknown, queued->running|settled|unknown, running->settled|unknown. Same-state rewrite of queued/running is allowed.
* `get(run_id) -> dict | None`: None when no file. Raises `StoreError` when the file is unreadable, the seal is wrong, `record["run_id"] != run_id`, or `binding(argv,cwd,commit) != record["binding"]`. Returns the record including seal.
* `all_records() -> (list[dict], list[str])`: verified records sorted by `seq`, and the run_ids that failed verification.
* `next_seq() -> int`: 1 + max seq over verified records (0 records -> 1).
* `output_path(run_id) -> Path` under `root/output/<run_id>.log`.

Record fields: run_id, seq, binding, argv, cwd, commit, task, purpose, units (int; 0 for nested), weight_requested, max_seconds,
state (queued|running|settled|unknown), outcome (None|exited|timed_out|lost_in_restart|stale_commit|launch_failed|interrupted),
exit_code (int|None), nested_in (run_id|None), backfill (bool), submitted_at, started_at, settled_at (epoch floats or None),
seconds (float|None, wall), unit_seconds (float|None = units*seconds), tokens (int), custody (None|"gone"|"uncertain"),
output_sha256, output_bytes, seal.

## admission.py — pure
`@dataclass(frozen=True) Entry(run_id, units, seq)`, `Holder(units, backfill)`.
`pick(queue, holders, capacity) -> (Entry, bool) | None`, queue in arrival order (list of Entry):
* free = capacity - sum(h.units)
* empty queue -> None. head = queue[0]. If head.units <= free -> (head, False).
* else (head cannot start): room = capacity - head.units - sum(h.units for h in holders if h.backfill).
  First entry in queue[1:] (arrival order) with units <= min(room, free) -> (entry, True). Else None.
  (This is the TOOLING6 backfill rule in src/otto/hostctl/heavy.py `_take`: a backfilled job never delays the head, because head + all backfilled jobs always fit within capacity.)
Callers clamp units to 1..capacity first.

## commit.py — git_commit_identity(cwd) -> str | None
`git -C cwd rev-parse HEAD`; None if cwd is not a git work tree or no commit. Clean tree -> the 40-hex sha. Dirty (git status --porcelain=v1 -z non-empty, untracked included) -> `"<sha>+dirty-<first 16 hex of sha256(git diff HEAD --binary output + for each untracked file (git ls-files -o --exclude-standard -z): name + NUL + file bytes)>"`. Timeouts 30s, subprocess with list argv.

## runner.py — Runner
```
Runner(pool, store, *, state_dir, resolve_commit=git_commit_identity, census_fn=None, environ=None,
       grace_seconds=1.0, clock=time.time, launch=None, poll_seconds=0.5)
```
* `pool`: herzchen.fleet.capacity.CapacityPool. Capacity of the runner = `pool.policy.heavy_headroom`. The runner is the sole heavy user of that pool. Never add a second ledger; never touch pool internals (only queue_heavy / claim_heavy / release_heavy / prune_dead_heavy / snapshot).
* `state_dir/latches/<run_id>.json` custody latches. `census_fn` default None -> custody's own census. `launch` default `Custody.launch` (looked up at call time).
* State kept in memory: `_queue` (list of Entry, arrival order), `_leases: dict[run_id, Lease]` (Lease: run_id, ticket, units, backfill, custody, children[list of run_ids], lock), one `threading.Condition`.
* `__init__` runs `reconcile()` before anything can be served. `start()` starts a ticker thread (pump every poll_seconds while the queue is non-empty); `stop()` stops the ticker, terminates every live lease's custody and settles those runs as state `unknown`, outcome `interrupted`.

### submit(request: Mapping, peer_pid: int|None = None) -> dict
request keys: argv (non-empty list of str, no NUL), cwd (existing dir; realpath it), weight (int, default 1; clamp to 1..capacity), task (str, default "untasked"), purpose (str, default first 120 chars of the joined argv), max_seconds (0 < x <= 86400, default 3600), request_id (optional, run-id regex).
Errors are returned, never raised: `{"ok": False, "error": "<code>", "detail": "..."}` with codes: bad_request, no_commit, binding_mismatch, evidence_invalid.
1. commit = resolve_commit(cwd); None -> no_commit. binding = store.binding(argv, cwd, commit). run_id = request_id or "run-" + uuid4().hex[:12].
2. Under the condition lock: if a record for run_id already exists: StoreError -> evidence_invalid (never launch); binding differs -> binding_mismatch; same binding -> return `{"ok": True, "run_id", "state": <stored state>, "existing": True, "binding", "commit"}` and launch NOTHING (this is the idempotent resubmit; a settled command never reruns).
3. Nested check (below). Write the queued record. If nested: no pool units; units 0; start it immediately (state running). Else append Entry to `_queue` and `pump()`.
4. Return `{"ok": True, "run_id", "state", "nested": bool, "binding", "commit"}`.

### Nested call recognition — by lease identity, never by environment
The runner never reads any environment variable from the client. `peer_pid` comes from the socket (kernel peer credentials). `_parent_lease(peer_pid)`: take a census snapshot (census_fn() or custody.census()); if None -> not nested (fail closed: counted as a standalone run). For each live lease (under its lock) `live = lease.custody.observe(snap)`; the peer is nested in that lease when `peer_pid in live` and `snap[peer_pid].birth == live[peer_pid]`. That covers a client that left the process group via setsid, because custody adopts descendants by parent pid. A nested run is launched by the daemon under its own Custody (so timeouts apply) with units 0, `nested_in=<parent run_id>`, and is registered in `parent.children`. When the parent lease ends (exit, timeout, stop), the runner terminates its still-running children and settles them `unknown`/`interrupted` if they have not settled. A nested run takes no pool units and adds no heavy seconds (it runs under the parent's units: counted once).

### pump()
Under the condition lock, loop: `pick(queue, holders, capacity)`; None -> stop. Else `ticket = pool.queue_heavy("runner:" + run_id, units, pid=None)`; `if not pool.claim_heavy(ticket)` (catch KeyError too): `pool.release_heavy(ticket)`, stop looping (retry on next pump). On success remove the entry from `_queue`, make a Lease (backfill flag from pick), and start `_execute` on a daemon thread. Call `pool.prune_dead_heavy()` first. The runner decides order and backfill; the pool only ever holds the one ticket the runner is starting, so pool order never disagrees.

### _execute(run_id) (thread)
1. Re-resolve the commit; if it differs from the record's commit -> settle state `unknown`, outcome `stale_commit`, exit_code None, never launched.
2. Persist record state `running` (started_at, backfill) BEFORE launching. (Crash between put and launch just becomes `unknown` on reconcile; it is never re-run.)
3. Launch with `Custody.launch(argv, latch_path=state_dir/latches/<run_id>.json, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdin=DEVNULL, stdout=<output file>, stderr=STDOUT)`. env = copy of `environ` (default os.environ) plus `RUNNER_USAGE_PATH=<state_dir>/usage/<run_id>.json`; never anything from the client. Launch OSError -> settle `unknown`, outcome `launch_failed`.
4. `process.wait(timeout=max_seconds)`. TimeoutExpired -> `custody.terminate(grace_seconds)`; outcome `timed_out`, exit_code 124. Otherwise `custody.release()` to sweep leftovers; outcome `exited`; exit_code = returncode if >= 0 else 128 + (-returncode). custody field = "gone" if the disposition is gone else "uncertain" (the latch is then kept for the next reconcile).
5. Read the usage file if present: JSON `{"tokens": N}` with N a non-negative int -> tokens, otherwise 0. Output file sha256 and byte count -> record.
6. seconds = clock() - started; unit_seconds = units * seconds. Persist the terminal record (state `settled`) FIRST, then under the condition lock remove the lease, `pool.release_heavy(ticket)` (not for nested), terminate/settle children, `notify_all()`, `pump()`.

### await_run(run_id, timeout=None) -> dict
Waits on the condition until `store.get(run_id)` is terminal or the timeout passes. Returns `{"ok": True, "done": True, "record": rec, "exit_code": code}` where code = rec.exit_code for state settled, `EXIT_UNKNOWN` (70) for state unknown. Unknown run -> `{"ok": False, "error": "unknown_run"}`. StoreError -> `{"ok": False, "error": "evidence_invalid"}`. Timeout elapsed -> `{"ok": True, "done": False, "state": ...}`.

### status(run_id=None) / report(task=None)
status -> `{"ok": True, "capacity", "used", "free", "holders": [{run_id, units, backfill, task, purpose, started_at}], "waiting": [{run_id, units, task, purpose}], "pool": pool.snapshot(), "record": <that run's record or None>}`.
report -> reads store.all_records(): per task `{runs, settled, unknown, seconds, unit_seconds, tokens}` plus `totals` (the same fields summed over ALL verified records; nothing else), and `invalid: [run_ids]` (never summed). Totals must equal the sum over the stored results exactly (round seconds to 3 places at write time, sum the stored numbers).

### reconcile() — before any launch
1. Verify every stored record; failures go to `self.invalid` and are left untouched.
2. For every `running` record: `resume_cleanup(latch_path, grace_seconds, census_fn)` (from custody; also run it for latch files with no matching running record), then settle the record state `unknown`, outcome `lost_in_restart`, exit_code None, custody from the disposition. NEVER relaunch.
3. For every `queued` non-nested record: re-resolve the commit; equal -> re-queue in `seq` order (it was never launched); different or None -> state `unknown`, outcome `stale_commit`. Queued nested records -> `unknown`/`lost_in_restart`.
4. Release any heavy lease the pool already holds (`pool.snapshot()["heavy"]["leases"]` -> `pool.release_heavy(ticket)`): at construction this runner owns none, so every one is a leftover of an earlier life.
5. Settled and unknown records are never touched.

## server.py
`RunnerServer(runner, socket_path)`: ThreadingMixIn + UnixStreamServer; the socket's parent dir is made 0700 if we create it, the socket file chmod 0600. If the path exists and a connect succeeds -> raise (already running); if stale -> unlink. One JSON object per line in, one JSON object per line out; request size cap 1 MiB; bad JSON -> `{"ok": False, "error": "bad_request"}`; unknown op -> `{"ok": False, "error": "unknown_op"}`. Ops: submit, await, status, report — nothing else (there is NO op that writes a result). Peer pid: macOS `sock.getsockopt(0, 2)` (SOL_LOCAL=0, LOCAL_PEERPID=2); Linux `SO_PEERCRED` unpacked with struct "3i" (pid, uid, gid). Passed to `runner.submit(req, peer_pid)`. Extra request keys such as "result", "state", "store", "exit_code" are ignored by submit (it builds the record itself).
`main(argv=None)`: `--socket PATH` (required), `--state-dir DIR` (required; the store is `<state-dir>/store`), `--capacity N` (default 3 = heavy_headroom), `--forbid-root PATH` (repeatable). Builds `CapacityPool(CapacityPolicy(heavy_headroom=N))` in memory, ResultStore, Runner (reconcile happens in the constructor, before the socket binds), runner.start(), serves until SIGTERM/SIGINT, then runner.stop().

## client.py
`RunnerUnavailable(RuntimeError)`. `RunnerClient(socket_path, timeout=None)`; `.call(request: dict) -> dict` connects, sends one JSON line, reads one JSON line; connection failure -> RunnerUnavailable.

## Exit codes
`EXIT_UNKNOWN = 70` (in runner.py, re-exported). 124 = timed out. Command exit codes pass through.

## Otto side (src/otto/runner_cli.py) — verbs `otto run submit|await|status|report|daemon`
`main(argv=None) -> int`. Global `--socket PATH` (default env OTTO_RUNNER_SOCKET, else `<OTTO_HOME or ~/.otto>/runner.sock`).
* `submit [--weight N] [--task T] [--purpose P] [--max-minutes M] [--request-id ID] [--cwd DIR] [--wait] -- CMD...` prints the submit response JSON; with `--wait` it then awaits and exits with the command's exit code.
* `await RUN_ID [--timeout S]` prints the await response JSON and exits with `exit_code` (the command's own code; 70 unknown; 3 if not done before --timeout; 69 when the runner is unreachable; 2 usage; 1 other errors).
* `status [RUN_ID]`, `report [--task T]` print JSON, exit 0 (1 on error response, 69 unreachable).
* `daemon --state-dir DIR [--capacity N]` runs `herzchen.fleet.runner.server.main` with the socket and `--forbid-root` set to the labs root it is given by `--forbid-root` (pass through).
